answer: To resist Sybil attacks, agents stake tokens into a graph verified via topological cut verifications. A game-theoretic multi-agent auditing protocol detects sparse cuts concealing fraudulent clusters, triggering stake slashing. As seen in the network atlas, valid cut sizes grow with cluster radius, imposing a superlinear attacker cost for Sybil expansion: forging a dark sable cluster requires locking exponential walnut reserves.
